# Context Pack: `cli-dispatch-exit-contract` — CLI dispatch and exit-code envelope contract Target: ultraplan-go @ 8eef70f4903b25580719960009a170945bdad9ad (frozen). Planning context: ultraplan-workspace @ ab12dc38059c9bf485f9aced9075bcd7d924cac5. Domain: operator-interfaces. Risk: high. Descriptive only — no defect judgments. ## 1. Purpose `cmd/ultraplan/main.go:18-43` wires OS argv/stdout/stderr, a signal context (`signal.NotifyContext` on SIGINT/SIGTERM, main.go:19), and the TUI/web runner adapters into `app.Run`, then exits with its integer return (`os.Exit`). `app.Run` (internal/app/app.go:88-178) is the single admission point for every invocation: it normalizes nil streams to `io.Discard` (stdout/stderr) or `os.Stdin` (stdin), defaults version and workdir, constructs the process-wide `runControlState` closed via defer (app.go:108-109), parses global flags, and dispatches one of 15 arms — `--help/-h`, `version`, and 13 command words (`init-workspace`, `defaults`, `skills`, `config`, `health`, `storage`, `run`, `project`, `sprint`, `study`, `tui`, `serve`, `code`) — at app.go:144-177; anything else is ExitUsage. The surface owns the numeric exit-class vocabulary (0-8, app.go:15-25), the stable-code strings derived from classes (`errorCode`, app.go:67-86), the classified-error wrapper that carries both a display string and an exit class (`classedError`, app.go:41-65), the stderr one-liner printer (`fail`, app.go:229-241), the shared JSON envelope writer (`json_output.go`), and the per-command renderers/flag grammars in `*_commands.go`. Scripts and agents consume three things: process exit codes, stdout bytes, and stderr bytes; docs/cli-reference.md declares those contracts. ## 2. Entrypoints and control flow ### 2.1 Global admission `parseGlobalFlags` (app.go:198-220) extracts only `--workspace ` / `--workspace=` (rejecting missing or dash-prefixed values) and passes all other tokens through in order; no other global flags exist. Empty argv, `--help`, `-h` print `renderHelp()` to stdout and exit 0 (app.go:140-146); unknown first token exits 2 with a pointer to `--help` (app.go:175-176). Every handler returns a single `error`; `failOrOK`/`fail` (app.go:222-241) print `err.Error()` as one stderr line and return the wrapped `classedError.class`, falling back to ExitError(1) for unclassed errors (including raw I/O write errors returned by handlers). `writeStatus` (app.go:243-248) returns ExitError if the stdout write itself fails. ### 2.2 Verb families - **Pure text inspectors** (no workspace mutation): `version` (app.go:147-148 → `renderVersion`), `config show [--json]` (config_commands.go:10-119; ~60 fixed `key: value` lines plus `(source: …)` provenance annotations; redaction applied before rendering), `project list|

status|

validate` (project_commands.go:10-75; validate findings are printed to **stderr**, project_commands.go:118-129, and any findings force ExitValidation). - **Workspace writers**: `init-workspace [--path --dry-run]` (workspace_commands.go), `defaults install [--path --dry-run --force]` (defaults_commands.go), `skills materialise [stage] [--path --dry-run --force]` accepting the `materialize` alias (skills_commands.go:17-23). All three print operation plans (`created/would create/overwrite/skip file …`) and use ExitWorkspace for failures. - **Durable-store door**: `run list|show|follow|cancel|diagnostics` (run_commands.go:19-40) — full behavior is the run-cli-observation pack's subject; this surface owns its arg parsing conventions (`std flag.FlagSet` with output discarded, `helpRequested` pre-check, `orderRunArgs` hand-rolled flag/positional reordering for show/follow/cancel/diagnostics, run_commands.go:463-481) and its error→class mapping `mapRunControlError` (403-414): ErrInvalidArgument→2, ErrNotFound→5, ErrConflict/ErrTerminal→8, everything else→6. - **Study/sprint product verbs** (§2.3-2.4): large hand-rolled positional+flag grammars over `study.Service` / `sprint.Service`. - **Frontends**: `tui` (tui_commands.go:21-61) and `serve` (serve_commands.go:18-99) build `dashboardUseCases`/`NewWebUseCases`, open the run-control repository, and delegate to injected runners; `serve` validates `--listen` as a numeric loopback IP:port *before* workspace discovery (ValidateLoopbackListen, serve_commands.go:119-139; test-enforced ordering serve_commands_test.go:51) and maps shutdown-time context cancellation to exit 0 (serve_commands.go:62-64, 92-97). - **Utility**: `storage migrate [--dry-run] [--json]` (storage_commands.go:33-140) imports study/sprint state files into SQLite and exits ExitPartial when any item failed (136-138); `code ... [--json] [--output]` (code_commands.go:19-78) maps extraction status Validation→5 / Partial→8. ### 2.3 Sprint verb grammar (sprint_commands.go) `runSprint` (28-566) requires ` `; `conformance-review` is aliased to `review` in-place (77-79). Help checks are position-sensitive (args[3]/args[4]). Per verb: - `status [--json]` (90-121): renders status; smoke-readiness failure categories `catalog`/`review_gate` downgrade the JSON `status` label to `"partial"` but still exit 0. - `metrics [--json]` (122-141): bare service DTO encoded directly (no envelope fields beyond the struct). - `validate ` (142-179): ten stages incl. execute/review/smoke; invalid stage → usage; failed validation → ExitValidation after printing findings. - `prompt [--explain]` (180-222): prints the rendered prompt verbatim to stdout; `--explain` emits explanation JSON instead. - `flow --to […]` (223-279): requires `--yes` for non-dry-run smoke targets (234-235); non-dry-run wraps work in `beginDurableCLICommand`; error classification ladder at 256-273: findings present → ExitValidation regardless of cause; else **`strings.Contains(err.Error(), "runtime")` → ExitRuntime** (269-272); else `mapSprintError`. - `verify […]` (280-328): same durable wrap; typed smoke errors go through `mapSmokeError`, others `mapSprintError`; assessment fail/blocked forces ExitValidation (325-327). The verify payload is emitted even on failure, with `status` taken from `result.Verification.Assessment` and an added `error` object from `stableCommandError` (313-318). - `execute […]` (329-368): durable wrap skipped for dry-run and for `--defer` (defer runs outside the durable boundary, 349-350); classification ladder 356-366: findings → 5; **`Contains(err.Error(), "failed tasks")` → ExitPartial**; **`Contains(err.Error(), "runtime")` → ExitRuntime**; else mapSprintError. - `qa [map|status|recover|cancel|run|resume]` (369-466): parser enforces flag/action compatibility (588-640, e.g., cancel requires `--run`, forbids `--shard`); run/resume take the durable path with QA writer-token handoff; progress callbacks print `[qa] …` to **stderr** with redacted messages (435-441); the JSON envelope `{schema_version, operation:"sprint.qa", status, result, error?}` is written to **stdout even on failure** (454-459), with `error` built by `stableQACommandError` (category, retryable, correlation_id, recovery, timestamp). - `review […]` (467-512): durable wrap unless dry-run; verdict fail or status blocked → ExitValidation; **`Contains(err.Error(), "runtime")` → ExitRuntime** (507-509); else mapSprintError. - `smoke […]` (513-562): `--yes` mandatory for non-dry-run (518-520); typed `mapSmokeError` decides everything (879-892): category cancellation→7, process/timeout/cleanup→6, all other typed categories→5; untyped falls back to mapSprintError; verdict fail/blocked → ExitValidation. Shared mappers: `mapSprintError` (944-963) orders `context.Canceled`→7, `DeadlineExceeded`→6, `ErrVerificationConflict`→8, flow-state and execute-state sentinels→5, project/sprint RefError→5, default→ExitWorkspace(4). `mapQACommandError` (662-679) maps canceled/deadline→**ExitPartial(8)** with codes `qa.cancelled`/`qa.deadline_exceeded`, QA-typed runtime/persistence→6 with codes `qa.`, other QA categories→5, fallback→mapSprintError. `stableCommandError` (1463-1470) reduces any classed error to `{code, message, recovery}` where message passes through `displaySafe` (usecases.go:251-278: config redaction + ANSI/control-char stripping). ### 2.4 Study verb grammar (study_commands.go, study_runs_commands.go) `runStudy` (26-120) routes `init | list | list | {summary, validate, status, runs, run-loop, run-all, run, synthesize, prompt}`; sub-verbs are matched positionally (`args[1]=="run-loop"` etc.). Runtime-backed verbs (`run-loop`, `run-all`, `run`, `synthesize`) wrap execution in `beginDurableCLICommand` and classify results afterwards: `classifyRunAllResult` (732-745) completed→0, cancelled→7, partial→8, runtime-failed→6, otherwise→5; `classifyExecutionResult` (933-948) completed/skipped→0, runtime-failed→6, cancelled→7, validation-failed/preflight-blocked→5, unknown status→ExitError(1). Read-only doors: `status [--json]` uses the shared envelope with `statusJSONResult` (status_json.go:67-145 — counts, redacted lock command, per-task usage/cost as `{known,value}` pairs, workspace-relative paths); `validate [--json]` uses the shared envelope with redacted checks and returns ExitValidation when failed (1012-1044); `summary`/`runs summary` regenerate artifacts and return 0 unless resolution/history sync fails. Error mappers: `mapStudyError`/`mapStudyPromptError`/`mapStudySummaryError` (RefError/config sentinels→5, default→4), `mapStudyRunLoopError` (locked→8, malformed/unsupported→5, else execution mapper), `mapStudyStatusError` (1162-1178 — missing/malformed→5, else→4, with a `displayError` wrapper whose display string has absolute paths rewritten relative via `strings.ReplaceAll`). ### 2.5 Durable acceptance coverage (dispatch-level contract) `beginDurableCLICommand` (durable_operations.go:49-60) opens the repository, accepts an outer operation row with an **empty alias digest** (so alias dedup is unreachable from CLI, durable_operations.go:55), claims it, appends a lifecycle-running event, and hands back a cancellation-aware context. CLI call sites: sprint flow/verify/execute/review/smoke/qa-run/qa-resume (6 textual call sites) and study run-loop/run-all/run/synthesize (4). Dry-run, prompt, validate, status, metrics, qa map/status/recover/cancel, storage, run-observation, and all foundation verbs skip acceptance. `finishDurableCLICommand` (86-91) joins the run error with `Finish`, which classifies the terminal outcome (ctx-done→cancelled, deadline→timed_out, err→failed, else succeeded) under a fresh 30 s `context.Background()` window so terminal persistence survives parent cancellation, and surfaces finish failure as a classed ExitRuntime error joined into the result. `TestEveryRuntimeBackedCLIEntryUsesDurableAcceptanceInventory` (run_control_inventory_test.go:11-55) pins these call-site counts and kind strings by reading the source files. ## 3. Inputs / outputs Inputs: `os.Args[1:]`; env vars read via `envLookup` (`ULTRAPLAN_WORKSPACE`, `ULTRAPLAN_STUDY_MODEL` studyModelOverride study_commands.go:183-188, QA/smoke settings via effective config, smoke `Getenv` injection sprint_commands.go:814-823); stdin for the three confirmation prompts (§5); filesystem state behind discovery/validation; wall clock (`timeNow` var, study_commands.go:1160, used in envelope timestamps and status reconciliation). Outputs, by stream: - **stdout**: help/version text; all human result renderers; all JSON envelopes and NDJSON (`run follow --json`); interactive prompts and their echoes for defaults/skills/run-loop-reset confirmations; `[run-loop]` task-progress lines (the documented exception to stderr-progress discipline, cli-reference.md:32); `serve` startup messages. - **stderr**: exactly one line per failed command via `fail()`; sanitized progress streams for sprint flow/verify/execute/review/smoke/qa and study run-all/run/synthesize (`[sprint]`, `[runtime]`, `[smoke]`, `[qa]` prefixes; redacted via `config.RedactValue`); project-validate findings; non-completed-task and warning summaries after study runs; serve diagnostics. - **exit code**: one of {0..8}; ExitError(1) is reachable only through write failures, unclassified handler errors, `serve`/`tui` runner failures, code-render failures, and the unknown-status arm of `classifyExecutionResult`. Envelope families (all schema_version 1): 1. Shared `writeJSON` envelope `{schema_version, command, workspace, status, generated_at, result}` (json_output.go:20-31): `config show`, `health`, `study validate`, `study status`, `run list/show/diagnostics` (diagnostics sets `status` to `string(health.Status)` rather than constant "ok"). 2. Ad-hoc command envelopes `{schema_version, operation, status, result, error?}` encoded inline: `sprint status/flow/verify/qa/review/smoke` (and `metrics` emits the bare DTO without wrapper fields). 3. Deterministic domain JSON: `code --json` (`codeextract.RenderJSON`), `storage migrate --json` (`storageMigrationResult` struct). Failure-path emission varies: health writes its envelope with status "fail" before returning the error (health_commands.go:46-50); sprint flow/verify/qa write failure envelopes best-effort (`_ =` discard of encode errors, e.g., sprint_commands.go:259, 318, 459); most other verbs emit nothing on stdout when failing. ## 4. Authoritative state None durable is owned here. This surface is projection/admission only: it creates no tables, holds no locks beyond what delegated layers acquire, and persists nothing except through delegated effects (files written by init/defaults/skills/study-init/code-output/prompt-output/storage-migrate; rows written via beginDurableCLICommand and runRepository; listener socket in serve). Process-local state: `runControlState` singleton (per-workspace repository+logger, closed at Run exit), the `durableOperationManager` created per accepted command (owned-operation map, control goroutine), and the injectable `timeNow`. The authoritative stores it touches belong to other surfaces: `.ultraplan/run-control.db` (run-journal-fencing), flow-state/execute-state/QA files (sprint-flow-state, sprint-qa-investigation), run-state.json (study-runloop-scheduler), product-state DB (product-state-mirror). ## 5. Invariants (as implemented) - One admission function; every exit path flows through `fail`/`writeStatus` so each command produces at most one stderr line and a single class from {0..8}. - Classified errors preserve their cause chain (`Unwrap`, app.go:48) so `errors.Is/As` ladders operate on original sentinels/typed errors while the class rides on the wrapper. - Stable code strings per class (`errorCode`); QA adds a finer `qa.` code vocabulary carried inside JSON payloads (phase3-json-schemas.md:35 closed list). - Interactive confirmations have no TTY detection anywhere: `confirmOverwriteDefaults` (defaults_commands.go:125-144), `confirmOverwriteSkills` (skills_commands.go:148-167), and `confirmRunLoopReplacement` (study_commands.go:277-316) read one line from configured stdin; EOF is tolerated (treated as a non-affirmative answer); non-"yes/y" answers keep existing files or refuse replacement (replacement refusal exits ExitPartial "replacement not confirmed", study_commands.go:314). Destructive non-interactive paths require explicit flags instead: `--force` (defaults/skills), `--reset --yes` (run-loop), `--yes` (smoke/flow-to-smoke/verify-to-smoke), `--force-review --override-reason` pairs enforced at parse time (sprint_commands.go:873-876, 1070-1072, 1187-1189). - Stream discipline as documented: runtime-backed sprint progress → stderr; final results → stdout; study run-loop progress → stdout by documented exception; human errors → stderr. - Durable acceptance precedes runtime work for exactly the inventory-pinned entry set; acceptance happens after parse/discover/config so malformed invocations never create runs. - Terminal proposal after cancellation uses a detached context, so a cancelled command still records its durable outcome when persistence is reachable. - Redaction before display on every renderer that embeds potentially sensitive values (`config.RedactValue` calls across config/health/study/sprint/QA renderers); `displaySafe` additionally strips ANSI escapes/control bytes for JSON-embedded messages. ## 6. Trust boundaries - All argv tokens, env vars, and stdin answers are untrusted admission input. They reach: workspace/config loading (validated downstream by config-inspection-health), file paths for init/defaults/skills/code-output/prompt-output (`--output` for study prompt is containment-checked via `workspace.ResolveInside`, study_commands.go:1409; `code --output` is not contained, only made absolute against workDir, code_commands.go:56-65), model refs (`--model`, passed through to runtime request construction), listen address (strictly validated loopback-only), and identifiers echoed into error strings (e.g., `%q` of unknown commands/stages). - Error text is inspected by classifiers: the sprint flow/execute/review ladders branch on substrings of `err.Error()` ("runtime", "failed tasks") produced by lower packages; everything else classifies via typed sentinel/`errors.As` matches. A parallel guard exists for the TUI/web operation path asserting free-form text does not affect classification there (sprint_error_test.go:29-41); the CLI substring branches are separate code. - Error text also reaches consumers: `fail()` prints `err.Error()` verbatim to stderr (causes are app-constructed; several embed user-supplied tokens quoted); JSON envelopes embed only `displaySafe`-processed messages; `stableCommandError`'s fixed `recovery` string is constant. - Confirmation prompts accept any stdin bytes; only exact `yes`/`y` (case-insensitive, trimmed) affirm. - The `serve` door inherits web-security-boundary controls; dispatch contributes the loopback-listen validation and never forwards raw argv further. ## 7. External effects & lifecycle semantics External effects per invocation can include: workspace scaffold/default/skill file creation or overwrite (with confirm/force gates); git clone subprocesses during `study init` (partial failures → ExitPartial with redacted clone output, study_init_commands_test.go:113); SQLite DB/schema creation (`storage migrate` non-dry-run opens runcontrol + productstate); durable run rows/events/terminals in run-control.db for accepted verbs; report/prompt/output file writes; a listening loopback socket and optional platform browser launch (`openBrowser`, main.go:45-62, exec of `open`/`rundll32`/`xdg-open` with 5 s timeout); TUI takeover of stdout. Cancellation semantics: the process-level context derives from SIGINT/SIGTERM. For durable-wrapped verbs, cancellation propagates through the accepted operation's child context; `Finish` records cancelled/timed_out terminals; `mapSprintError` yields exit 7 for plain cancellation while the QA command path deliberately yields exit 8 with code `qa.cancelled` (both behaviors test-pinned). `serve` treats shutdown cancellation as success (exit 0) after drain. `run follow` ends observation-only on ctx-done (exit 0). Non-durable verbs simply unwind; partial side effects (e.g., half-written scaffolds) are not compensated anywhere in this layer. Retry semantics: none at this layer — no handler retries on failure; retryability is expressed only as data (`retryable` booleans in QA error payloads; typed store-error flags consumed elsewhere). Restart semantics: stateless between invocations; every invocation re-runs discovery/config and (for repository-opening verbs) startup reconcile owned by deeper surfaces. The surface owns the numeric exit-class vocabulary (0-8, app.go:15-25), the stable-code strings derived from classes (`errorCode`, app.go:67-86), the classified-error wrapper that carries both a display string and an exit class (`classedError`, app.go:41-65), the stderr one-liner printer (`fail`, app.go:229-241), the shared JSON envelope writer (`json_output.go`), and the per-command renderers/flag grammars in `*_commands.go`. Scripts and agents consume three things: process exit codes, stdout bytes, and stderr bytes; docs/cli-reference.md declares those contracts. ## 2. Entrypoints and control flow ### 2.1 Global admission `parseGlobalFlags` (app.go:198-220) extracts only `--workspace ` / `--workspace=` (rejecting missing or dash-prefixed values) and passes all other tokens through in order; no other global flags exist. Empty argv, `--help`, `-h` print `renderHelp()` to stdout and exit 0 (app.go:140-146); unknown first token exits 2 with a pointer to `--help` (app.go:175-176). Every handler returns a single `error`; `failOrOK`/`fail` (app.go:222-241) print `err.Error()` as one stderr line and return the wrapped `classedError.class`, falling back to ExitError(1) for unclassed errors (including raw I/O write errors returned by handlers). `writeStatus` (app.go:243-248) returns ExitError if the stdout write itself fails. ### 2.2 Verb families - **Pure text inspectors** (no workspace mutation): `version` (app.go:147-148 → `renderVersion`), `config show [--json]` (config_commands.go:10-119; ~60 fixed `key: value` lines plus `(source: …)` provenance annotations; redaction applied before rendering), `project list|

status|

validate` (project_commands.go:10-75; validate findings are printed to **stderr**, project_commands.go:118-129, and any findings force ExitValidation). - **Workspace writers**: `init-workspace [--path --dry-run]` (workspace_commands.go), `defaults install [--path --dry-run --force]` (defaults_commands.go), `skills materialise [stage] [--path --dry-run --force]` accepting the `materialize` alias (skills_commands.go:17-23). All three print operation plans (`created/would create/overwrite/skip file …`) and use ExitWorkspace for failures. - **Durable-store door**: `run list|show|follow|cancel|diagnostics` (run_commands.go:19-40) — full behavior is the run-cli-observation pack's subject; this surface owns its arg parsing conventions (`std flag.FlagSet` with output discarded, `helpRequested` pre-check, `orderRunArgs` hand-rolled flag/positional reordering for show/follow/cancel/diagnostics, run_commands.go:463-481) and its error→class mapping `mapRunControlError` (403-414): ErrInvalidArgument→2, ErrNotFound→5, ErrConflict/ErrTerminal→8, everything else→6. - **Study/sprint product verbs** (§2.3-2.4): large hand-rolled positional+flag grammars over `study.Service` / `sprint.Service`.

Authoritative state 61: 62: None durable is owned here. This surface is projection/admission only: it creates no tables, holds no locks beyond what delegated layers acquire, and persists nothing except through delegated effects (files written by init/defaults/skills/study-init/code-output/prompt-output/storage-migrate; rows written via beginDurableCLICommand and runRepository; listener socket in serve). 568: func stripFlag(args []string, flag string) ([]string, bool) {
569: 	out := make([]string, 0, len(args))
570: 	found := false
571: 	for _, arg := range args {
572: 		if arg == flag {
573: 			found = true
574: 			continue
575: 		}
576: 		out = append(out, arg)
577: 	}
578: 	return out, found
579: }

588: func parseSprintQAArgs(args []string) (sprintQACommand, error) {
589: 	command := sprintQACommand{Action: "run"}
590: 	if len(args) > 0 {

1240: 	fmt.Fprintln(deps.stdout, "Stages:")
1241: 	for _, stage := range status.Stages {

1463: func stableCommandError(err error) map[string]string {
1464: 	code := "internal.error"
1465: 	var classed classedError
1466: 	if errors.As(err, &classed) {
1467: 		code = classed.Code()
1468: 	}
1469: 	return map[string]string{"code": code, "message": displaySafe(err.Error()), "recovery": "Inspect stderr and sprint status, repair the reported cause, then retry."}
1470: }

1472: func stableQACommandError(mapped, cause error, result QAResult) map[string]any {
1473: 	base := stableCommandError(mapped)
1474: 	out := map[string]any{
1475: 		"code": base["code"], "message": base["message"], "recovery": base["recovery"],
1476: 		"severity": "error", "operation": "sprint.qa", "component": "sprint",
1477: 	}
1478: 	if typed, ok := sprint.AsQAError(cause); ok {
1479: 		out["category"] = string(typed.Category)
1480: 		out["recovery"] = typed.Recovery
1481: 		out["retryable"] = typed.Category == sprint.QAErrorConflict || typed.Category == sprint.QAErrorRuntimeUnavailable
1482: 	}
1483: 	if result.RunID != "" {
1484: 		out["correlation_id"] = result.RunID
1485: 	} else if result.OperationalAttemptID != "" {
1486: 		out["correlation_id"] = result.OperationalAttemptID
1487: 	}
1488: 	if !result.UpdatedAt.IsZero() {
1489: 		out["timestamp"] = result.UpdatedAt.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano)
1490: 	}
1491: 	return out
1492: }

232: 		case <-owned.stop:
233: 			return

254: 			}

268: 	owned := m.owned[runID]

270: 	m.mu.Unlock()

273: 	}

277: 		if appendErr != nil && runErr == nil {
278: 			runErr = appendErr
279: 		}
280: 		owned.omitted = 0
281: 	}
282: 	owned.eventMu.Unlock()
283: 	close(owned.stop)

285: 	owned.cancel()

reasoning_details.text:
Key observations in durable_operations.go:

1. `Finish` (line 71-84): `state := OperationComplete; if c.accepted.Context.Err() != nil { state = OperationCancelled }`. Note: `accepted.Context` is the operationCtx derived from parent ctx (deps.ctx = signal context). If the user pressed Ctrl+C, ctx cancelled → Finish records TerminalCancelled — good.

BUT: consider the case where the run itself failed because of a *deadline* on operationCtx? Fine.

2. **Critical race/liveness**: `FinishOperation` line 283-284: `close(owned.stop); <-owned.done`. The control goroutine's select includes `<-ctx.Done()` and `<-owned.stop`. When stop is closed, control goroutine returns, closing done. OK, no deadlock... unless controlOperation is blocked in `m.repository.Snapshot(ctx, ...)` — it uses operationCtx which is still alive until line 285 cancel(). If repository.Snapshot blocks (e.g., SQLite lock held by another process), `<-owned.done` waits indefinitely — no timeout on join! The 30s timeout applies only to the terminal proposal afterwards. A stuck control-goroutine DB call → CLI hangs forever despite Ctrl+C? Well if ctx is cancelled, Snapshot(ctx) should return promptly with ctx.Err. But if the DB call is stuck in a cgo/syscall not honoring ctx... sqlite driver usually honors context. Moderate.

3. **`Finish` uses `state == OperationCancelled` based on `c.accepted.Context.Err() != nil`** — but wait: what if the run error is nil AND context was cancelled exactly after successful completion? Then outcome=cancelled even though work completed. Edge.

4. **More important**: In `Finish`, when `runErr != nil` AND context cancelled, state=OperationCancelled takes priority; then switch: `errors.Is(runErr, DeadlineExceeded)` first → timed_out. Hmm: if runErr is context.Canceled and state==OperationCancelled → TerminalCancelled ✓.

But notice asymmetry: `finishDurableCLICommand(durable, err)` joins runErr + Finish error. If Finish fails (e.g., terminal proposal rejected due to fence conflict), the joined error is `errors.Join(runErr, classifiedCause(ExitRuntime,...))`. Then classification ladders: e.g., sprint flow: findings→5 else contains "runtime"→6... The finish error message "run-control.finish: ..." contains "runtime"? No — contains "run-control.finish". errors.Join produces newline-separated messages! `errors.Join(err1, err2).Error()` = "err1\nerr2". So the stderr output of fail() would be MULTIPLE lines for any durable command whose run errored AND finish errored, or where runErr itself is a Join. Also mapSprintError uses errors.Is on the joined error — works through Join.

Wait, more common case: run fails with normal error E; Finish succeeds → returns just E. Fine, one line. Only when Finish also fails do we get two lines. Rare.

BUT there's a much more common multi-line path: `classifiedCause(ExitRuntime, err, "run-control.finish")` wraps a joined error? No—Finish returns that directly; finishDurableCLICommand joins runErr+that. So flow error path with both failing → stderr has ≥2 lines. Minor contract deviation ("exactly one stderr line").

5. **AcceptOperation alias digest ""**: `if err != nil && digest != "" && errors.Is(...)` — with empty digest, conflict falls to generic error. Pack noted dedup unreachable from CLI — every retry creates a new run row. That means `sprint flow --to execute` retried after failure creates a NEW durable run each time — no idempotency at acceptance level. Is that a defect? For scripts doing retry loops, each attempt is separately tracked — arguably intended. Not clearly a defect by itself.

6. `controlOperation` heartbeat/reconcile use `ctx` = operationCtx. On cancellation via owned.stop (from FinishOperation), fine.

7. **RecordOperationEvent coalescing** — used by web/TUI mostly; CLI progress doesn't route through here except controlledRuntimeFor maybe. Check later.

8. **The QA writer-token fence function**: `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` — Go 1.21+. OK.

Now the big question about `Finish` ordering bug: `finishDurableCLICommand(durable, err)`:
```go
return errors.Join(runErr, command.Finish(runErr))
```
If runErr is nil and Finish fails → returns ExitRuntime-classified "run-control.finish" error even though the operation succeeded. Documented unknown #5 in pack. It's real: a fully-successful sprint flow exits 6 if terminal persistence hiccups (e.g., transient SQLITE_BUSY). Observable bad outcome: script treats success as runtime failure and re-runs an already-completed destructive-ish flow. Flow is idempotent-ish though (stage artifacts). Hmm severity medium, confidence high on behavior; whether it's a defect depends on doctrine — pack lists it as unknown. I can elevate it with concrete trigger: proposeRunTerminalWithRetry fails after retries. Let me check proposeRunTerminalWithRetry and how likely failure is. Also note: FinishOperation returns err from proposeRunTerminalWithRetry — check that function in run_control.go.

9. Also `AcceptOperation` line 116: Claim failure → return error WITHOUT recording terminal — the accepted row stays "prepared/running?" Actually Accept succeeded (row created), claim failed → row left in prepared state with no owner and no terminal. Next invocation accepts ANOTHER row. Accumulating orphan rows — operability concern for `run list`. Deeper surface owns reconcile presumably. Not dispatch-level.

10. Line 121-129: appendRunEventWithRetry failure → proposes persistence_lost terminal. OK good.

11. **`beginDurableCLICommand` error class**: `classifiedCause(ExitRuntime, ...)` — so acceptance failure → exit 6 ✓ documented.

12. Note `AcceptOperation(deps.ctx, ...)` uses deps.ctx (signal ctx). If Ctrl+C during accept → accept fails with context.Canceled wrapped → classifiedCause(ExitRuntime) → exit 6, NOT exit 7! Cancellation during the acceptance window yields ExitRuntime("run-control.accept: ... context canceled") instead of ExitCancel(7). Hmm — is that wrong? mapRunControlError maps ErrInvalidArgument→2 etc.; beginDurableCLICommand hard-classifies everything to 6. A script that distinguishes "user cancelled" (7) from "infra broke" (6) would misread. Concrete: SIGINT arrives between parse and accept-complete → exit 6 with code provider.runtime. Plausible but is 6 wrong? The docs say 6 = runtime/persistence failure; a cancelled accept didn't persist anything... The generic convention elsewhere: cancellation → 7. This is a genuine classification inconsistency, though narrow window. Medium-low.

Also `sprintRuntimeService` failures AFTER accept are finished properly (finishDurableCLICommand called) ✓ — those return classified ExitConfig/ExitRuntime; Finish(runErr): state=failed (ctx not cancelled) → TerminalFailed. Then error propagates: e.g. config error class 3 preserved since finishDurableCLICommand joins runErr (classed config) with nil. Good.

Wait — actually check: `flowService, err = sprintRuntimeService(deps, root); if err != nil { return finishDurableCLICommand(durable, err) }` → joins config-classed err with Finish result (nil normally) → errors.Join(err, nil)? errors.Join ignores nils → returns just err ✓. Class preserved (3).

13. **`Finish` when `c.accepted.Context.Err() != nil` but runErr==nil and the run actually completed successfully just as SIGINT arrived**: outcome cancelled although side effects committed. Script sees exit... well FinishOperation returns nil error, so runErr remains nil → command exits 0 while durable row says cancelled. Divergence between recorded outcome and exit code. Narrow race, low.

14. RecordOperationEvent: `owned.cancel()` on event append failure cancels the operation context — liveness choice, deeper surface.

Now let me look at run_control.go (runControlState, runRepository, appendRunEventWithRetry, proposeRunTerminalWithRetry) and study_commands.go classifiers. And check concurrency of Progress callbacks inside internal/sprint (review workers parallel?).

150: 	return controlledRuntime{base: base, repository: repository, owner: deps.runControl.owner}, nil
151: }

159: func (r controlledRuntime) StartRun(ctx context.Context, req runtimepkg.Request) (runtimepkg.Result, error) {
160: 	target := targetFromRuntimeRequest(req)
161: 	correlation := runcontrol.Correlation{
162: 		ProductRunID:  boundedSafe(string(runcontrol.ParentRun(ctx))),
163: 		ProductTaskID: boundedSafe(req.TraceID),
164: 	}
165: 	snapshot, err := r.repository.Accept(ctx, runcontrol.Acceptance{
166: 		Target:        target,
167: 		Correlation:   correlation,
168: 		ProductStatus: "accepted",
169: 	})
170: 	if err != nil {
171: 		return runtimepkg.Result{}, fmt.Errorf("durable run acceptance failed: %w", err)
172: 	}
173: 	attempt, _, err := r.repository.Claim(ctx, runcontrol.Claim{
174: 		RunID: snapshot.RunID, Owner: r.owner, Lease: runControlLease, Correlation: correlation,
175: 	})
176: 	if err != nil {
177: 		return runtimepkg.Result{}, fmt.Errorf("durable run ownership failed: %w", err)
178: 	}
179: 	fence := runcontrol.Fence{
180: 		RunID: snapshot.RunID, AttemptID: attempt.ID, OwnerID: r.owner.ID,
181: 		FencingGeneration: attempt.FencingGeneration,
182: 	}
183: 
184: 	runCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
185: 	defer cancel()
186: 	req.Metadata = cloneRuntimeMetadata(req.Metadata)
187: 	req.Metadata["run_control_run_id"] = string(snapshot.RunID)
188: 	configuredOnEvent := req.OnEvent
189: 	var eventMu sync.Mutex
190: 	var persistenceErr error
191: 	var progressKey string
192: 	var progressCommittedAt time.Time
193: 	var progressOmitted uint64
194: 	var progressOmittedFirst time.Time
195: 	var progressOmittedLast time.Time
196: 	setPersistenceErr := func(value error) {
197: 		eventMu.Lock()
198: 		defer eventMu.Unlock()
199: 		if persistenceErr == nil {
200: 			persistenceErr = value
201: 			cancel()
202: 		}
203: 	}
204: 	req.OnEvent = func(event runtimepkg.Event) {
205: 		eventMu.Lock()
206: 		defer eventMu.Unlock()
207: 		if persistenceErr != nil {
208: 			return
209: 		}
210: 		draft := runtimeEventDraft(req, event)
211: 		eventAt := event.Time.UTC()
212: 		if eventAt.IsZero() {
213: 			eventAt = time.Now().UTC()
214: 		}
215: 		// Content-aware coalescing: only collapse identical progress payloads within the window.
216: 		// Reasoning/text deltas and tool calls have distinct payload hashes and will not coalesce.
217: 		hash := payloadHash(draft.Payload)
218: 		key := string(draft.Type) + "\x00" + draft.Stage + "\x00" + draft.Task + "\x00" + hash
219: 		elapsed := eventAt.Sub(progressCommittedAt)
220: 		if draft.Type == runcontrol.EventProgress && key == progressKey && elapsed >= 0 && elapsed < runcontrol.ProgressCoalesceWindow {
221: 			if progressOmitted == 0 {
222: 				progressOmittedFirst = eventAt
223: 			}
224: 			progressOmitted++
225: 			progressOmittedLast = eventAt
226: 			return
227: 		}
228: 		if progressOmitted > 0 {
229: 			if draft.Omission == nil {
230: 				draft.Omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: "equivalent progress coalesced"}
231: 			}
232: 			draft.Omission.Count += progressOmitted
233: 			draft.Omission.FirstAt = &progressOmittedFirst
234: 			draft.Omission.LastAt = &progressOmittedLast
235: 			progressOmitted = 0
236: 		}
237: 		if _, _, appendErr := appendRunEventWithRetry(runCtx, r.repository, fence, draft); appendErr != nil {
238: 			persistenceErr = fmt.Errorf("persist runtime event: %w", appendErr)
239: 			cancel()
240: 			return
241: 		}
242: 		if draft.Type == runcontrol.EventProgress {
243: 			progressKey = key
244: 			progressCommittedAt = eventAt
245: 		}
246: 		if configuredOnEvent != nil {
247: 			configuredOnEvent(event)
248: 		}
249: 	}
250: 
251: 	controlDone := make(chan struct{})
252: 	go func() {
253: 		defer close(controlDone)
254: 		ticker := time.NewTicker(runcontrol.OwnerTickInterval)
255: 		defer ticker.Stop()
256: 		lastHeartbeat := time.Now()
257: 		lastReconcile := time.Now()
258: 		for {
259: 			select {
260: 			case <-runCtx.Done():
261: 				return
262: 			case now := <-ticker.C:
263: 				snapshot, err := r.repository.Snapshot(runCtx, fence.RunID)
264: 				if err != nil {
265: 					if runCtx.Err() != nil {
266: 						return
267: 					}
268: 					setPersistenceErr(fmt.Errorf("poll durable run control: %w", err))
269: 					return
270: 				}
271: 				if snapshot.Cancellation.State == runcontrol.CancellationRequested {
272: 					if _, _, err := r.repository.AcknowledgeCancellation(runCtx, fence); err != nil {
273: 						setPersistenceErr(fmt.Errorf("acknowledge durable cancellation: %w", err))
274: 						return
275: 					}
276: 					cancel()
277: 					return
278: 				}
279: 				if now.Sub(lastHeartbeat) >= runcontrol.HeartbeatInterval {
280: 					if _, err := r.repository.Heartbeat(runCtx, fence, runControlLease); err != nil {
281: 						if runCtx.Err() != nil {
282: 							return
283: 						}
284: 						setPersistenceErr(fmt.Errorf("persist owner heartbeat: %w", err))
285: 						return
286: 					}
287: 					lastHeartbeat = now
288: 				}
289: 				if now.Sub(lastReconcile) >= runcontrol.ReconciliationInterval {
290: 					if _, err := r.repository.Reconcile(runCtx, runcontrol.NativeProcessProbe{}, runcontrol.ReconcileOptions{}); err != nil {
291: 						if runCtx.Err() != nil {
292: 							return
293: 						}
294: 						setPersistenceErr(fmt.Errorf("reconcile durable runs: %w", err))
295: 						return
296: 					}
297: 					lastReconcile = now
298: 				}
299: 			}
300: 		}
301: 	}()
302: 	result, runErr := r.base.StartRun(runCtx, req)
303: 	eventMu.Lock()
304: 	if persistenceErr == nil && progressOmitted > 0 {
305: 		_, _, appendErr := appendRunEventWithRetry(runCtx, r.repository, fence, runcontrol.EventDraft{
306: 			Type: runcontrol.EventOmission,
307: 			Omission: &runcontrol.Omission{
308: 				Reason: "equivalent progress coalesced", Count: progressOmitted,
309: 				FirstAt: &progressOmittedFirst, LastAt: &progressOmittedLast,
310: 			},
311: 		})
312: 		if appendErr != nil {
313: 			persistenceErr = fmt.Errorf("persist progress omission: %w", appendErr)
314: 		}
315: 	}
316: 	eventMu.Unlock()
317: 	cancel()
318: 	<-controlDone
319: 	eventMu.Lock()
320: 	persistErr := persistenceErr
321: 	eventMu.Unlock()
322: 	if persistErr != nil {
323: 		terminalCtx, terminalCancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
324: 		_, _, terminalErr := proposeRunTerminalWithRetry(terminalCtx, r.repository, fence, runcontrol.TerminalProposal{
325: 			Outcome: runcontrol.TerminalPersistenceLost, Reason: "durable event persistence failed", ProposedBy: r.owner.ID,
326: 		})
327: 		terminalCancel()
328: 		if terminalErr != nil {
329: 			return result, errors.Join(persistErr, terminalErr)
330: 		}
331: 		return result, persistErr
332: 	}
333: 
334: 	outcome, reason := terminalOutcome(result, runErr, ctx)
335: 	terminalCtx, terminalCancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
336: 	defer terminalCancel()
337: 	if _, _, err := proposeRunTerminalWithRetry(terminalCtx, r.repository, fence, runcontrol.TerminalProposal{
338: 		Outcome: outcome, Reason: reason, ProposedBy: r.owner.ID,
339: 	}); err != nil {
340: 		return result, errors.Join(runErr, fmt.Errorf("persist terminal run outcome: %w", err))
341: 	}
342: 	return result, runErr
343: }
344: 
345: func appendRunEventWithRetry(ctx context.Context, repository runcontrol.Repository, fence runcontrol.Fence, draft runcontrol.EventDraft) (runcontrol.Event, runcontrol.Snapshot, error) {
346: 	deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
347: 	for {
348: 		event, snapshot, err := repository.Append(ctx, fence, draft)
349: 		if err == nil || !retryableRunControlError(err) || !time.Now().Before(deadline) {
350: 			return event, snapshot, err
351: 		}
352: 		if err := waitRunControlRetry(ctx, deadline); err != nil {
353: 			return runcontrol.Event{}, runcontrol.Snapshot{}, err
354: 		}
355: 	}
356: }
357: 
358: func proposeRunTerminalWithRetry(ctx context.Context, repository runcontrol.Repository, fence runcontrol.Fence, proposal runcontrol.TerminalProposal) (runcontrol.Snapshot, bool, error) {
359: 	for {
360: 		snapshot, won, err := repository.ProposeTerminal(ctx, fence, proposal)
361: 		if err == nil || !retryableRunControlError(err) {
362: 			return snapshot, won, err
363: 		}
364: 		if err := waitRunControlRetry(ctx, time.Now().Add(250*time.Millisecond)); err != nil {
365: 			return runcontrol.Snapshot{}, false, err
366: 		}
367: 	}
368: }
369: 
370: func retryableRunControlError(err error) bool {
371: 	return errors.Is(err, runcontrol.ErrUnavailable) || errors.Is(err, runcontrol.ErrBusy)
372: }
373: 
374: func waitRunControlRetry(ctx context.Context, deadline time.Time) error {
375: 	wait := time.Until(deadline)
376: 	if wait > 100*time.Millisecond {
377: 		wait = 100 * time.Millisecond
378: 	}
379: 	if wait <= 0 {
380: 		return context.DeadlineExceeded
381: 	}
382: 	timer := time.NewTimer(wait)
383: 	defer timer.Stop()
384: 	select {
385: 	case <-ctx.Done():
386: 		return ctx.Err()
387: 	case <-timer.C:
388: 		return nil
389: 	}
390: }

392: func targetFromRuntimeRequest(req runtimepkg.Request) runcontrol.Target {
393: 	target := runcontrol.Target{
394: 		Kind:      boundedSafe(req.PromptRef.OwnerKind),
395: 		Operation: boundedSafe(req.PromptRef.Purpose),
396: 		Project:   boundedSafe(req.Metadata["project"]),
397: 		Sprint:    boundedSafe(req.Metadata["sprint"]),
398: 		Study:     boundedSafe(req.Metadata["study"]),
399: 		Stage:     boundedSafe(req.Metadata["stage"]),
400: 		Task:      boundedSafe(firstSafeValue(req.Metadata["task"], req.Metadata["task.kind"], req.Metadata["coverage"])),
401: 	}
402: 	if target.Kind == "" {
403: 		if target.Study != "" {
404: 			target.Kind = "study"
405: 		} else if target.Sprint != "" {
406: 			target.Kind = "sprint"
407: 		} else {
408: 			target.Kind = "runtime"
409: 		}
410: 	}
411: 	if target.Operation == "" {
412: 		target.Operation = boundedSafe(firstSafeValue(target.Stage, req.Metadata["task.kind"], req.PromptRef.ID, "runtime"))
413: 	}
414: 	return target
415: }

417: func runtimeEventDraft(req runtimepkg.Request, event runtimepkg.Event) runcontrol.EventDraft {
418: 	eventType := runcontrol.EventProgress
419: 	lowerType := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(event.Type))
420: 	lowerKind := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(event.Kind))
421: 	switch lowerType {
422: 	case "warning", "warn", "error":
423: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventWarning
424: 	case "artifact", "file":
425: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventArtifact
426: 	case "finding":
427: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventFinding
428: 	case "message", "text", "output", "assistant_text", "reasoning_text", "reasoning", "content", "delta":
429: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventMessage
430: 	default:
431: 		// Kind-based fallback: reasoning and message kinds should be visible as message, not coalesced progress.
432: 		switch lowerKind {
433: 		case "message", "reasoning", "assistant", "assistant_text", "reasoning_text":
434: 			eventType = runcontrol.EventMessage
435: 		case "tool", "tool_use", "tool_call", "tool_call_update":
436: 			// Tools stay as progress but with distinct payload so coalescing can distinguish.
437: 			eventType = runcontrol.EventProgress
438: 		}
439: 	}
440: 	payload := map[string]string{
441: 		"runtime_event_id": boundedSafe(event.ID),
442: 		"runtime_run_id":   boundedSafe(event.RunID),
443: 		"session_id":       boundedSafe(event.SessionID),
444: 		"type":             boundedSafe(event.Type),
445: 		"kind":             boundedSafe(event.Kind),
446: 	}
447: 	if lowerKind == "tool" || lowerKind == "tool_use" || lowerKind == "tool_call" || lowerKind == "tool_call_update" {
448: 		captureToolObservation(payload, event.Payload)
449: 	}
450: 	// Preserve safe observable payload fields into durable storage for observability.
451: 	// Deny sensitive keys and truncate values to runcontrol-safe limits.
452: 	// Flatten one level of nesting so tool/action names buried in maps are surfaced as top-level payload keys
453: 	// that the run timeline JS expects (payload.tool, payload.action, payload.title, etc.).
454: 	for key, value := range event.Payload {
455: 		if isSensitivePayloadKey(key) {
456: 			continue
457: 		}
458: 		normalized := strings.TrimSpace(key)
459: 		if normalized == "" || len(normalized) > 128 || strings.ContainsAny(normalized, "\x00\r\n") {
460: 			continue
461: 		}
462: 		if normalized == "type" || normalized == "kind" {
463: 			continue
464: 		}
465: 		if nested, ok := value.(map[string]any); ok {
466: 			for subKey, subVal := range nested {
467: 				if isSensitivePayloadKey(subKey) {
468: 					continue
469: 				}
470: 				subNorm := strings.TrimSpace(subKey)
471: 				if subNorm == "" || len(subNorm) > 128 || strings.ContainsAny(subNorm, "\x00\r\n") {
472: 					continue
473: 				}
474: 				if _, exists := payload[subNorm]; exists {
475: 					continue
476: 				}
477: 				// Promote common observable sub-keys; namespace the rest to avoid collisions.
478: 				promote := map[string]bool{"tool": true, "title": true, "detail": true, "text": true, "delta": true, "content": true, "message": true, "action": true, "state": true, "status": true, "native_type": true, "line": true}
479: 				targetKey := subNorm
480: 				if !promote[subNorm] {
481: 					targetKey = normalized + "_" + subNorm
482: 					if len(targetKey) > 128 {
483: 						continue
484: 					}
485: 				}
486: 				if _, exists := payload[targetKey]; exists {
487: 					continue
488: 				}
489: 				str := payloadValueString(subVal)
490: 				if strings.TrimSpace(str) == "" {
491: 					continue
492: 				}
493: 				if len(payload) >= 30 {
494: 					break
495: 				}
496: 				payload[targetKey] = boundedPayloadValue(str)
497: 			}
498: 			// Also keep a compact stringified top-level for debugging if not promoted.
499: 			if len(payload) < 30 {
500: 				if _, exists := payload[normalized]; !exists {
501: 					str := payloadValueString(value)
502: 					if strings.TrimSpace(str) != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(str, "[map omitted") {
503: 						payload[normalized] = boundedPayloadValue(str)
504: 					}
505: 				}
506: 			}
507: 			continue
508: 		}
509: 		str := payloadValueString(value)
510: 		if strings.TrimSpace(str) == "" {
511: 			continue
512: 		}
513: 		if len(payload) >= 30 {
514: 			break
515: 		}
516: 		if _, exists := payload[normalized]; exists {
517: 			continue
518: 		}
519: 		payload[normalized] = boundedPayloadValue(str)
520: 	}
521: 	// Ensure the most useful display keys are always present even if nested.
522: 	for _, want := range []string{"tool", "action", "title", "detail", "text", "delta"} {
523: 		if _, ok := payload[want]; ok {
524: 			continue
525: 		}
526: 		if v := findNestedString(event.Payload, want); v != "" {
527: 			payload[want] = boundedPayloadValue(v)
528: 		}
529: 	}
530: 	omission := (*runcontrol.Omission)(nil)
531: 	if event.RawPresent || event.RawOmitted {
532: 		reason := firstSafeValue(event.RawOmissionReason, "runtime payload omitted by safe persistence policy")
533: 		omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: boundedSafe(reason), Count: 1}
534: 	} else if len(event.Payload) > len(payload)-5 {
535: 		// Payload had more fields than we persisted (truncated/omitted keys) – record for diagnostics but don't hide persisted fields.
536: 		omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: boundedSafe("runtime payload truncated to safe observable fields"), Count: 1}
537: 	}
538: 	return runcontrol.EventDraft{
539: 		Type: eventType, Scope: runcontrol.EventScopeRuntime,
540: 		Stage: boundedSafe(req.Metadata["stage"]), Task: boundedSafe(firstSafeValue(req.Metadata["task"], req.Metadata["task.kind"])),
541: 		Kind: payload["kind"], Tool: payload["tool"], Action: payload["action"],
542: 		Reason: payload["reason"], Detail: firstSafeValue(payload["detail"], payload["title"]),
543: 		Payload: payload, Omission: omission,
544: 	}
545: }

547: func isSensitivePayloadKey(key string) bool {
548: 	lower := strings.ToLower(key)
549: 	for _, marker := range []string{"secret", "token", "password", "authorization", "cookie", "api_key", "apikey", "credential", "auth"} {
550: 		if strings.Contains(lower, marker) {
551: 			return true
552: 		}
553: 	}
554: 	return false
555: }
556: 
557: func findNestedString(payload map[string]any, want string) string {
558: 	for _, v := range payload {
559: 		if m, ok := v.(map[string]any); ok {
560: 			if s, ok := m[want].(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(s) != "" {
561: 				return s
562: 			}
563: 			// One more level deep (common for opencode part.state structures)
564: 			for _, inner := range m {
565: 				if innerMap, ok := inner.(map[string]any); ok {
566: 					if s, ok := innerMap[want].(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(s) != "" {
567: 						return s
568: 					}
569: 				}
570: 			}
571: 		}
572: 	}
573: 	return ""
574: }
575: 
576: func payloadValueString(value any) string {
577: 	switch v := value.(type) {
578: 	case string:
579: 		return v
580: 	case []byte:
581: 		if len(v) == 0 {
582: 			return ""
583: 		}
584: 		return string(v)
585: 	case bool:
586: 		if v {
587: 			return "true"
588: 		}
589: 		return "false"
590: 	case int:
591: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
592: 	case int8:
593: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
594: 	case int16:
595: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
596: 	case int32:
597: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
598: 	case int64:
599: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
600: 	case uint, uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64:
601: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
602: 	case float32, float64:
603: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%v", v)
604: 	case map[string]any, map[string]string, []any, []string:
605: 		// Encode structured values compactly.
606: 		encoded, err := jsonMarshalTruncated(v)
607: 		if err != nil {
608: 			return fmt.Sprintf("%v", v)
609: 		}
610: 		return encoded
611: 	default:
612: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%v", v)
613: 	}
614: }
615: 
616: func jsonMarshalTruncated(v any) (string, error) {
617: 	encoded, err := json.Marshal(v)
618: 	if err != nil {
619: 		return "", err
620: 	}
621: 	return string(encoded), nil
622: }

624: func captureToolObservation(out map[string]string, payload map[string]any) {
625: 	for target, aliases := range map[string][]string{
626: 		"tool_call_id": {"tool_call_id", "toolCallId", "call_id", "callID"},
627: 		"tool_name":    {"tool_name", "toolName", "tool", "name"},
628: 		"tool_status":  {"tool_status", "status", "phase"},
629: 	} {
630: 		if value := findNestedPayloadValue(payload, aliases, 0); value != nil {
631: 			if text, ok := value.(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(text) != "" {
632: 				out[target] = boundedPayloadValue(text)
633: 			}
634: 		}
635: 	}
636: 	for target, aliases := range map[string][]string{
637: 		"tool_arguments": {"tool_arguments", "arguments", "args", "input", "parameters"},
638: 		"tool_result":    {"tool_result", "result", "output", "content"},
639: 		"tool_error":     {"tool_error", "error"},
640: 	} {
641: 		value := findNestedPayloadValue(payload, aliases, 0)
642: 		if value == nil {
643: 			continue
644: 		}
645: 		encoded, err := json.Marshal(redactObservableValue(value))
646: 		if err == nil && string(encoded) != "null" {
647: 			out[target] = boundedPayloadValue(string(encoded))
648: 		}
649: 	}
650: 	if out["tool"] == "" {
651: 		out["tool"] = out["tool_name"]
652: 	}
653: }
654: 
655: func findNestedPayloadValue(value any, aliases []string, depth int) any {
656: 	if depth > 5 {
657: 		return nil
658: 	}
659: 	switch typed := value.(type) {
660: 	case map[string]any:
661: 		for _, key := range aliases {
662: 			if found, ok := typed[key]; ok && found != nil {
663: 				return found
664: 			}
665: 		}
666: 		keys := make([]string, 0, len(typed))
667: 		for key := range typed {
668: 			keys = append(keys, key)
669: 		}
670: 		sort.Strings(keys)
671: 		for _, key := range keys {
672: 			if found := findNestedPayloadValue(typed[key], aliases, depth+1); found != nil {
673: 				return found
674: 			}
675: 		}
676: 	case []any:
677: 		for _, item := range typed {
678: 			if found := findNestedPayloadValue(item, aliases, depth+1); found != nil {
679: 				return found
680: 			}
681: 		}
682: 	}
683: 	return nil
684: }
685: 
686: func redactObservableValue(value any) any {
687: 	switch typed := value.(type) {
688: 	case map[string]any:
689: 		redacted := make(map[string]any, len(typed))
690: 		for key, item := range typed {
691: 			if isSensitivePayloadKey(key) {
692: 				redacted[key] = "[REDACTED]"
693: 			} else {
694: 				redacted[key] = redactObservableValue(item)
695: 			}
696: 		}
697: 		return redacted
698: 	case []any:
699: 		redacted := make([]any, len(typed))

Progress callbacks are all invoked from single (consumer) goroutines — no concurrent invocation. So the missing-mutex hypothesis for QA/review/smoke/flow progress callbacks is disproven. `renderSprintRuntimeProgress` has a mutex because runtime events come from the OpenCode event stream goroutines presumably.

But wait — is the flow/runtime progress (`renderSprintRuntimeProgress`, with mutex) called concurrently? It's attached via WithRuntimeProgress and used in StartRun events... The mutex suggests yes. Fine, that one has a mutex.

However there IS still an interleaving hazard: progress writes to stderr happen while the main goroutine may simultaneously write the final JSON envelope to stdout — different streams, no conflict. And within stderr: during `qa run`, the only stderr writer is the progress callback + fail() at end (after run completes). OK.

reasoning_details.text:
So `Adapter.StartRun` maps ctx.Canceled → Result{Status:"cancelled", Error{Category:"cancellation"}} + error. So study.RunAnalysis on mid-run cancellation: runErr != nil, runtimeResult.Error.Category == "cancellation" → statusForRuntimeFailure → ExecutionStatusCancelled → exit 7 ✓. Good counter-evidence — the common path is fine.

The narrow early-cancel window: if SIGINT lands before `a.runtime.StartRun(ctx,...)` even starts (e.g., during prepareRuntimeStore or toAgentwrapRequest), StartRun returns (Result{RuntimeStorePath}, err) with zero Status and nil Error → statusForRuntimeFailure → RuntimeFailed → exit 6 instead of 7. Also the controlledRuntime wrapper's Accept failure path returns Result{} entirely → same outcome. Window is small (ms), but for a long-running orchestration CLI, scripts retrying on 6 vs treating 7 as user-stop matters. This is a real but low-severity classification gap: "cancellation during runtime startup is reported as provider.runtime (6) rather than workflow.cancelled (7)". Confidence high on code path; reachability moderate.

reasoning_details.text:
Key insight for the substring ladder: when a runtime stage fails, the error returned is the raw runtime error from `startPlanningStageRun` — e.g., an `*agentwrap.SDKError`. Its Error() string is whatever the SDK error formats as. Whether it contains "runtime" depends on message content (e.g., "opencode runtime exited..."). So the flow ladder's `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "runtime")` is the ONLY thing distinguishing exit 6 from exit 4 for genuine provider failures. If a provider failure's message doesn't contain "runtime" (e.g., "connection refused", "401 unauthorized"), the CLI exits 4 (workspace) instead of 6 (runtime). That's the flip side of substring sniffing: misclassification in BOTH directions.

Conversely: validation-ish errors containing "runtime": e.g., "generated requirements.md failed validation" no. What about `repairGeneratedArtifact` errors? Or "persist runtime session for execute task" → contains "runtime" → 6 ✓ correct.

Concrete misfire candidate for "runtime" sniff on flow: `flow.go:139` returns error "code-context sprint workspace creation failed" WITH findings → findings branch wins → 5 ✓ fine.

What about a *cancellation* during flow? err = context.Canceled wrapped by SDK? Adapter.StartRun maps to SDKError with Cause=context.Canceled; errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) still true via Cause? mapSprintError checks errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) FIRST — but wait, in the CLI flow ladder, the order is:
1. findings → 5
2. contains "runtime" → 6
3. mapSprintError → cancellation check → 7

If a cancelled run's error message happens to contain "runtime" (very likely! e.g. SDKError message includes category/operation strings like "run cancelled"... does it contain "runtime"? The agentwrap SDKError.Error() format unknown), then Ctrl+C during flow yields 6 instead of 7. Let me check agentwrap.SDKError.Error() format. agentwrap is an external module? Check go.mod / vendor.

328: 	}

332: 	}
333: 	for _, snapshot := range page.Runs {

351: 	}

371: 	}

reasoning_details.text:
run_commands.go observations:

1. **`run follow` busy-polls with `time.Second` sleeps and NO liveness on missed wakeups** — fine for CLI.

2. **`mapRunControlError`**: cancellation of deps.ctx during repository call → default → ExitRuntime(6)! e.g., `run list` interrupted by Ctrl+C mid-query → exit 6 "provider.runtime" instead of 7 or 0. Hmm, but run follow explicitly handles ctx.Done → 0 (line 188-192). For the others (list/show/cancel/diagnostics), a Ctrl+C landing exactly during the DB query yields exit 6 with message "run-control...: context canceled". Window small; queries fast. Low.

3. **`orderRunArgs` bug candidate**: For valued flags (`--reason`, `--after`), it moves flag+value ahead. But what about a *positional* that equals a flag name? E.g., run-id literally "--json"? Not real. What about `--after` as LAST arg without value: `isFlag` true → flags gets "--after", no value follows (i+1 == len) → flag.Parse will error "flag needs an argument" ✓ usage.

Subtle: `run show -- --json`? "--" is not recognized flag → positional; flag.Parse treats "--" as terminator and remaining args as positional — but orderRunArgs already moved --json to front: ["--json","--"] → parse: --json flag consumed, then "--" terminates → NArg=1, Arg(0)="--"? Actually flag.Parse stops at "--" and excludes it? Go's flag package: parsing stops at first non-flag arg OR "--"; the "--" itself is not included in Args(). Wait: fs.Parse(["--json","--"]) → after --json, sees "--", sets args = args[1:] → remaining [] → NArg=0 → usage error "expected '<run-id>'". Edge case only.

4. **`writeRunSupportExport`**: writes file with O_EXCL — fails if exists → mapRunControlError default → ExitRuntime(6) for "file exists"?? A user-facing usage-ish error ("support export path already exists") mapped to exit 6 runtime. Minor misclassification: os.OpenFile EEXIST → ExitRuntime. Also permission denied → 6. Eh, arguably runtime-ish. Skip.

5. `run diagnostics --support-export relative/path` — written relative to cwd, fine.

Now let me look at workspace/defaults/skills commands + usecases.go displaySafe + operations.go OperationRequest kinds. Then tests. Then I'll evaluate the flow --json divergence and other candidates more carefully.

Pack lists prompts under stdout without flagging. It's a design choice; scripts using --force skip it. Not a finding.

# CLI Reference

This release includes study commands and governed sprint planning, execute, resumable automated review, integrated `verify`, focused review reruns, review-gated deep smoke, opt-in Git publication after completed stages, the terminal dashboard, and a loopback-only browser dashboard with guarded operations and SSE progress. Issue management, general Git automation beyond stage publication and sprint worktree creation, and hosted services remain deferred.

## Global Usage

```text
ultraplan [--workspace <path>] [command]
```

Global flags:

- `--workspace <path>`: use an explicit workspace path.
- `-h`, `--help`: show help.

Workspace discovery order is explicit flag, `ULTRAPLAN_WORKSPACE`, then current directory ancestry containing `ultraplan.yml`.

## Exit Classes

The CLI uses numeric process statuses:

- `0`: success.
- `1`: internal or write error.
- `2`: usage error.
- `3`: configuration error.
- `4`: workspace or filesystem error.
- `5`: validation/reference error.
- `6`: runtime/provider error.
- `7`: cancellation.
- `8`: partial completion.

Human-readable errors are printed to stderr. JSON commands use documented envelopes or deterministic command-specific JSON described below. Runtime-backed study and sprint commands also stream sanitized progress while preserving final result output. Standalone, run-all, and sprint progress uses stderr so stdout remains machine-readable; the durable study run-loop retains its task-progress stream on stdout. Progress includes lifecycle, provider progress, tool, validation, retry/fallback, permission, warning, and terminal events; message bodies and raw provider payloads are not printed.

## Commands

### `ultraplan init-workspace`

```text
ultraplan init-workspace [--path <dir>] [--dry-run]
```

Creates the minimal required workspace scaffold: `README.md`, `ultraplan.yml`, and `studies/`. The README includes common workspace commands. `--dry-run` prints planned operations without writing files.

Built-in prompts and templates are embedded in the CLI and are not required in the workspace.

### `ultraplan skills materialise`

```text
ultraplan skills materialise [all|stage] [--path <dir>] [--dry-run] [--force]
```

Writes manually invoked sprint-stage skills to
`.agents/skills/ultraplan-<stage>/`. With no selection, all eleven skills are
materialised. Supported stages are `reconcile`, `requirements`, `code-context`, `sprint-index`,
`technical-handbook`, `area-reasoning`, `reasoning`, `plan`, `execute`,
`review`, and `smoke`.

Each generated skill includes `SKILL.md` and `agents/openai.yaml`. Implicit
invocation is disabled. The `SKILL.md` embeds the canonical stage prompt and
adds interactive prerequisite checks, explicit proposal-only behavior,

`--dry-run` creates the byte-stable current map without a runtime, durable acceptance, or state write. Start and resume require current execute and Conformance Review evidence, accept and claim a durable run before child work, and optionally focus one current map-owned shard. Commands, paths, permissions, fingerprints, IDs, prompts, and theory content are product-owned. There are no caller flags for model or budgets. Workspace configuration may select the model and lower product limits.

`status` is read-only. `cancel` sends an explicit request through durable run control; closing a terminal or browser session does not cancel work. `recover` is runtime-free but may reconcile an interrupted/stale pointer, digest, bounded flow summary, or retention state. Resume always creates a new durable owner and never adopts an old runtime session.

Text says `Read-only QA completed` when bounded work ends. This is not a pass verdict. Theory outcomes are `confirmed`, `refuted`, `invalid`, `inconclusive`, `blocked`, `cross_shard`, and `not_applicable`; none is automatically an issue. QA cannot change the separate Conformance Review verdict.

With `--json`, success or failure is one object with `schema_version: 1`, `operation: "sprint.qa"`, `status`, `result`, and an optional stable `error`. The result carries phase and freshness separately from run lifecycle, cancellation, terminal result, Conformance Review status/verdict/freshness, fingerprints, coverage, effective limits, bounded shards, outcome totals, blocker, and next action. Usage errors use exit 2, configuration errors 3, validation/stale/policy errors 5, runtime or persistence failures 6, and cancellation or deadline partial results 8.

QA configuration uses normal precedence: product default, `ultraplan.yml`, then environment. Invalid workspace or environment values stop configuration loading. Integer limits and durations must be positive and cannot exceed the listed hard maximum. A default equal to its maximum can still be lowered.

7:Review, smoke, verify, and sprint status expose the applicable subset of:
===
# Phase 3 JSON Schemas

Phase 3 JSON is versioned with `schema_version: 1`. Additive fields may be introduced without a version change; existing field meanings and enum values are stable for version 1.

## Common verification fields

Review, smoke, verify, and sprint status expose the applicable subset of:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | integer | Schema major version; currently `1`. |
| `project`, `sprint` | string | Resolved governed identity. |
| `execution_status` | string | Lifecycle fact such as `ready`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, or `cancelled`. |
| `verdict` | string | Evidence verdict; distinct from execution status. |
| `stale` | boolean | Whether current inputs differ from recorded evidence. |
| `assessment` | string | Deterministic combined verification assessment. |
| `artifact` | string | Contained workspace-relative Markdown artifact path. |
| `diagnostics` | array | Bounded, redacted operator-safe diagnostics. |
| `next_action` | string | Required recovery or continuation action. |

## Conformance Review

The existing `review` JSON fields and `sprint.review` operation remain unchanged; Conformance Review is the human label. Review additionally exposes the review fingerprint, coverage summaries, finding counts, runtime/model facts where known, and resumable attempt state. `pass`, `pass_with_findings`, `fail`, and `blocked` are verdicts, not process statuses.

## Read-only QA

CLI QA uses one envelope: `schema_version`, `operation: "sprint.qa"`, `status`, `result`, and optional `error`. HTTP wraps the same typed result in the standard API success/error envelope. QA fields are additive to sprint status.

The CLI envelope is a stable JSON surface. Consumers must accept additive result fields while preserving the meanings of `schema_version`, `operation`, `status`, `result`, and `error`. QA error codes use the closed `qa.*` category names below. The result includes durable run and operational attempt IDs when the command accepted runtime-backed work.

The QA result contains project/sprint identity; `phase`; `fresh` and reasons; semantic attempt, durable run, operational attempt, and fencing correlation; run lifecycle and terminal result; governed-input, implementation, review, map, and policy fingerprints; independent `conformance_review_status`, `conformance_review_verdict`, and `conformance_review_fresh`; changed/covered counts; effective limits; bounded shard summaries; outcome totals; blocker; cancellation; and next action. Shard and theory resources embed the same summary plus one focused record. Synthesis adds validated challenger inputs, deduplication groups, contradictions, interactions, blockers, outcome totals, parent-linked follow-up shards, and its next action. Challenger records reference current theories and cannot alter their outcomes.

Closed phase values are `missing`, `mapped`, `queued`, `running`, `synthesizing`, `completed`, `blocked`, `cancelled`, `interrupted`, `stale`, and `invalid`. Closed theory outcomes are `confirmed`, `refuted`, `invalid`, `inconclusive`, `blocked`, `cross_shard`, and `not_applicable`. Phase, freshness, run lifecycle, cancellation, terminal result, and Conformance Review verdict are distinct; `completed` is not a pass verdict.

Stable QA errors use `qa.unknown_schema`, `qa.invalid_state`, `qa.stale_input`, `qa.permission_denied`, `qa.budget_exhausted`, `qa.conflict`, `qa.persistence_failure`, and `qa.runtime_unavailable`. Trusted CLI and durable-operation results retain a safe cause and recovery action. HTTP query responses keep those codes but use bounded public messages: invalid governed state is `422`, ownership conflict is `409`, and persistence or runtime unavailability is `503`.

Detailed filesystem state is strict schema v1 in the local `qa-v1` ID namespace:

```text
projects/<project>/sprints/<sprint>/verification/state.json
projects/<project>/sprints/<sprint>/verification/attempts/<qa-v1-attempt-id>/map.json
projects/<project>/sprints/<sprint>/verification/attempts/<qa-v1-attempt-id>/shards/<qa-v1-shard-id>.json
projects/<project>/sprints/<sprint>/verification/attempts/<qa-v1-attempt-id>/synthesis.json
```

`state.json` contains the current phase, freshness fingerprints, attempt and artifact pointers/digests, bounded counts, run/cancellation/blocker facts, next action, and update time. Maps freeze budgets, source traces, target/Git identity, coverage, shard definitions, and policy/catalog fingerprints. Shards retain attempts, safe evidence summaries, approved-check summaries, and complete falsifiable theories. `flow-state.json` contains only the bounded `QAFlowSummary` pointer projection.

| Artifact | Required identity and lifecycle fields | Referenced or bounded content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state.json` | `schema_version`, project, sprint, phase, freshness, current attempt, run correlation, update time | map and synthesis paths/digests, shard counts, outcome counts, blocker, cancellation, next action |
| `map.json` | `schema_version`, `qa-v1` map ID, semantic attempt ID, project, sprint, input and policy fingerprints | effective limits and sources, target/Git identity, coverage ownership, immutable shard definitions, governed artifact references |
| shard record | `schema_version`, `qa-v1` shard ID, attempt ID, kind, phase | assigned and context paths, approved checks, bounded attempts, usage and cost when known, evidence summaries, theories, blocker |
| `synthesis.json` | `schema_version`, `qa-v1` synthesis ID, map ID | theory IDs, challenge records, deduplication, contradictions, interactions, blockers, outcome counts, parent-linked follow-up shards, next action |

Verification IDs are deterministic only inside schema v1 and the selected project and sprint. A reader must not compare them as global content IDs. Unknown `qa-v1` record fields, invalid scoped IDs, pointer escape, digest mismatch, or a schema major other than 1 makes the detailed state unreadable until explicit recovery or a compatible migration is available.

No QA state migration ships in this release. Future migrations must be ordered pure transforms with fixtures for the prior and next forms. They must preserve the current attempt, last readable records, review fingerprint, run correlation, and pointer digests or stop without replacing the prior state. Operators should keep the existing files intact, use a compatible UltraPlan binary, and run `qa recover` only after that binary recognizes the stored major version.

`flow-state.json` remains schema version 2 and now permits the optional bounded `qa` member. A pre-Sprint-36 binary uses strict unknown-field decoding, so it rejects a QA-published flow state as malformed. It does not delete or rewrite the file. Mixed-version processes must not share a workspace after QA publication. Upgrade every process that can touch the workspace before publishing QA state. This accepted compatibility limit is specific to the single-host deployment model and is frozen by compatibility tests.

The QA result contains project/sprint identity; `phase`; `fresh` and reasons; semantic attempt, durable run, operational attempt, and fencing correlation; run lifecycle and terminal result; governed-input, implementation, review, map, and policy fingerprints; independent `conformance_review_status`, `conformance_review_verdict`, and `conformance_review_fresh`; changed/covered counts; effective limits; bounded shard summaries; outcome totals; blocker; cancellation; and next action. Shard and theory resources embed the same summary plus one focused record. Synthesis adds validated challenger inputs, deduplication groups, contradictions, interactions, blockers, outcome totals, parent-linked follow-up shards, and its next action. Challenger records reference current theories and cannot alter their outcomes.

Closed phase values are `missing`, `mapped`, `queued`, `running`, `synthesizing`, `completed`, `blocked`, `cancelled`, `interrupted`, `stale`, and `invalid`. Closed theory outcomes are `confirmed`, `refuted`, `invalid`, `inconclusive`, `blocked`, `cross_shard`, and `not_applicable`. Phase, freshness, run lifecycle, cancellation, terminal result, and Conformance Review verdict are distinct; `completed` is not a pass verdict.

Stable QA errors use `qa.unknown_schema`, `qa.invalid_state`, `qa.stale_input`, `qa.permission_denied`, `qa.budget_exhausted`, `qa.conflict`, `qa.persistence_failure`, and `qa.runtime_unavailable`. Trusted CLI and durable-operation results retain a safe cause and recovery action. HTTP query responses keep those codes but use bounded public messages: invalid governed state is `422`, ownership conflict is `409`, and persistence or runtime unavailability is `503`.

Detailed filesystem state is strict schema v1 in the local `qa-v1` ID namespace:

```text
projects/<project>/sprints/<sprint>/verification/state.json
projects/<project>/sprints/<sprint>/verification/attempts/<qa-v1-attempt-id>/map.json
projects/<project>/sprints/<sprint>/verification/attempts/<qa-v1-attempt-id>/shards/<qa-v1-shard-id>.json
projects/<project>/sprints/<sprint>/verification/attempts/<qa-v1-attempt-id>/synthesis.json
```

`state.json` contains the current phase, freshness fingerprints, attempt and artifact pointers/digests, bounded counts, run/cancellation/blocker facts, next action, and update time. Maps freeze budgets, source traces, target/Git identity, coverage, shard definitions, and policy/catalog fingerprints. Shards retain attempts, safe evidence summaries, approved-check summaries, and complete falsifiable theories. `flow-state.json` contains only the bounded `QAFlowSummary` pointer projection.

| Artifact | Required identity and lifecycle fields | Referenced or bounded content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state.json` | `schema_version`, project, sprint, phase, freshness, current attempt, run correlation, update time | map and synthesis paths/digests, shard counts, outcome counts, blocker, cancellation, next action |
| `map.json` | `schema_version`, `qa-v1` map ID, semantic attempt ID, project, sprint, input and policy fingerprints | effective limits and sources, target/Git identity, coverage ownership, immutable shard definitions, governed artifact references |
| shard record | `schema_version`, `qa-v1` shard ID, attempt ID, kind, phase | assigned and context paths, approved checks, bounded attempts, usage and cost when known, evidence summaries, theories, blocker |
| `synthesis.json` | `schema_version`, `qa-v1` synthesis ID, map ID | theory IDs, challenge records, deduplication, contradictions, interactions, blockers, outcome counts, parent-linked follow-up shards, next action |

Verification IDs are deterministic only inside schema v1 and the selected project and sprint. A reader must not compare them as global content IDs. Unknown `qa-v1` record fields, invalid scoped IDs, pointer escape, digest mismatch, or a schema major other than 1 makes the detailed state unreadable until explicit recovery or a compatible migration is available.

No QA state migration ships in this release. Future migrations must be ordered pure transforms with fixtures for the prior and next forms. They must preserve the current attempt, last readable records, review fingerprint, run correlation, and pointer digests or stop without replacing the prior state. Operators should keep the existing files intact, use a compatible UltraPlan binary, and run `qa recover` only after that binary recognizes the stored major version.

`flow-state.json` remains schema version 2 and now permits the optional bounded `qa` member. A pre-Sprint-36 binary uses strict unknown-field decoding, so it rejects a QA-published flow state as malformed. It does not delete or rewrite the file. Mixed-version processes must not share a workspace after QA publication. Upgrade every process that can touch the workspace before publishing QA state. This accepted compatibility limit is specific to the single-host deployment model and is frozen by compatibility tests.

But it does contradict "message bodies and raw provider payloads are not printed" in spirit — that sentence is about progress streams. The flow envelope includes ErrorDetail "fork/exec ..." etc. flow isn't declared stable. I'll mention briefly under the envelope-family finding, not standalone.

Also observed: stderr got MULTIPLE lines? No — stderr here has progress lines (documented) + final one-line error ✓.

Hard mid-run. Alternative: check code path again... FinishOperation error → proposeRunTerminalWithRetry fails when e.g. DB file locked by another process or disk full. Hard to simulate quickly; code path is clear though. Actually I CAN simulate: run two processes where one holds a write lock on run-control.db during the finish window... complex timing. reasoning_details.text:
The command hung past 90s even though SIGINT was sent at 4s. Interesting — that itself suggests a liveness problem on cancellation! Let me investigate: after SIGINT, the flow should cancel (agentwrap probe killed via CommandContext?) and finishDurableCLICommand should record terminal. But the process kept running for 85+ more seconds. Possibly:
- agentwrap probe uses its own timeouts/retries not bound to ctx?
- The retry policy had attempts with delays; ctx cancellation should stop it.
- Or `wait $PID` in that bash didn't return because process ignored SIGINT? signal.NotifyContext captures SIGINT → ctx cancelled. Then StartRun's select sees ctx.Done → run.Cancel(context.Background()) then waits up to 5s for waitCh... The stub sleeps 60s ignoring SIGTERM? run.Cancel probably kills the process. Hmm.

Wait, maybe the earlier attempt (first bg attempt) left an orphan `ultraplan` process still running (sleep 60), holding the sprint mutation lock! The second invocation would block on acquireMutationContext waiting for the lock file. That's why it hung — lock contention with the orphaned first process, NOT necessarily a cancellation hang.

Let me check for leftover processes and clean up, then redo carefully with setsid and checking ps output.

But in my repro I sent SIGINT to the *subshell* PID! `( ... ; echo $? > code ) & PID=$!` — PID is the SUBSHELL's pid, not the ultraplan process! kill -INT hit the subshell; bash subshells die on SIGINT? Hmm — but earlier (first test) the same pattern: `kill -INT $(cat pid)` where pid was from `echo $!` after `cmd & echo $! > pid` — that WAS the ultraplan process directly (`/tmp/opencode/ultraplan ... & echo $! > pid`). But this last run: SIGINT to subshell → likely NOT delivered to ultraplan at all → natural completion → exit 4, terminal failed. Consistent.
